subject: Tenant request spike — attribution, temporary cap adjustment, and remediation steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <ops@novushealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant request spike — attribution, temporary cap adjustment, and remediation steps

Hi Carlos / Novus ops team,

We detected a short window of elevated 429s affecting a subset of your traffic starting ~07:45 PDT today. Initial triage points to a tenant-to-namespace routing discrepancy that caused some of your spike traffic to be accounted against a global rate namespace rather than your dedicated tenant bucket. That caused a rapid enforcement of a rate cap for requests routed through the affected path.

What we've done so far:
- Scoped the surface: ~07:45–08:05 PDT, ~0.6% of requests returned 429, concentrated on batch inference endpoints.
- Applied a temporary tenant cap adjustment to allow traffic through while we fix routing (24-hour window).
- Pulled the request timeline and a KV-cache sample for your review (attached).

Planned next steps (technical):
1) Immediate config patch to correct namespace mapping (we plan to deploy in the next 60 minutes).
2) Reconcile counted tokens and create a provisional credit for the affected window; we will follow up with the exact credit amount once reconciliation completes.
3) Formal postmortem with timeline, root cause, and permanent guardrails (delivery target: EOD +2 business days).

Can you confirm if your team saw increased client-side retrying or queueing errors in the same window? I'd like to schedule a 30-minute sync today if that works — proposing 10:30 PDT.

Attachments: redwood_incident_timeline_20270721.csv, kv-cache-sample.txt

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos@novushealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:28:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant request spike — attribution, temporary cap adjustment, and remediation steps

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the heads up. We did see a spike in client-side 429s around 07:50 and several of our workers started exponential backoff which caused job queuing on our side.

Can you confirm how long the temporary cap will remain? If you are pushing a patch that will take an hour, we want to know whether to keep workers paused or to resume and rely on retries. Also please confirm the process and timeline for the credits — this incident did impact pipeline processing for a set of patient triages this morning.

—Carlos
Ops Lead, Novus Health
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Carlos Mendez <ops@novushealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:05:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant request spike — attribution, temporary cap adjustment, and remediation steps

Carlos — quick technical summary and plan from the infra side: 

Sean wrote: 
> Root cause: a recently deployed routing rule (safe-deploy 20270720) introduced a fallback mapping for legacy model routes. Under burst conditions the fallback path erroneously matched Novus tenant headers and routed ~7000 requests into a global namespace. The enforcement layer then applied the global namespace limits, producing 429 replies for requests that would otherwise have used the tenant bucket.
>
> Immediate remediation: we are rolling a targeted config patch (config-patch.diff attached) to tighten header matching and ensure tenant-header priority. This patch is small and will be rolled first to a canary, then to global (expected 35–45 minutes end-to-end).
>
> Short-term mitigation: Kimberly has already applied a temporary cap adjustment for Novus (effective now +24h) so traffic should flow. We will monitor for regressions and can extend the window if you prefer.

Credit and reconciliation:
- We will reconcile token accounting for the affected window and propose a provisional credit within 24 hours. Final reconciliation and credit posting within 3 business days.

Proposed actions for Novus ops:
- If you have time-critical queues, you can resume workers; we expect the temporary cap to avoid additional 429s. If you prefer to avoid any risk, pause for 1 hour until the patch completes.
- We're ready to join your runbook call now or at 10:30 PDT.

Attachments: config-patch.diff

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos@novushealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant request spike — attribution, temporary cap adjustment, and remediation steps

Appreciate the quick follow-through. We resumed workers at ~09:20 yesterday and saw normal throughput after that; the main disruption window for our pipelines was ~07:45–09:10 PDT.

We accept the provisional credit proposal — please include the exact token/usage offset when you reconcile. Also a +1 for the proposed postmortem; our security/compliance team will want the timeline and the guardrails you add to prevent routing regressions.

If you can send a calendar invite for a short review with your infra leads, we'll join. Thanks again for the fast response and for the temporary cap.

—Carlos
Ops Lead, Novus Health
